About this program
Biology, Doctor of Philosophy
Explore life's biggest questions through original research spanning molecules, organisms, populations, and ecosystems while developing the expertise to advance discovery in the biological sciences.
Ask bigger questions
You will learn to design and conduct original research, collect and analyze data, select appropriate quantitative methods and models, and interpret your findings within a broader scientific context. Through independent inquiry, rigorous analysis, and scientific communication, you will build the skills to evaluate evidence, defend your approach, and share your findings with scientific and professional audiences.
This program is a strong fit if you are curious about how living systems work, motivated by unanswered questions, and ready to take greater ownership of your research. You will graduate prepared to contribute new knowledge in your field and pursue research-focused careers in academia, government, industry, and other scientific settings.
Choose the doctoral pathway that best supports your research interests and goals. You can build broad expertise through advanced coursework in the biological sciences or pursue the Ecology, Evolution and Conservation Biology (EECB) emphasis for a more focused interdisciplinary experience. Both options allow you to shape your doctoral training around your research while building the expertise needed for independent scientific inquiry.
Ecology, Evolution and Conservation Biology - Explore how ecological and evolutionary processes shape populations, communities, and ecosystems. You will combine ecological and evolutionary theory with hands-on research while developing expertise in ecological sampling, statistical analysis, and evidence-based approaches to understanding biodiversity. Through your research, you will investigate questions related to invasive species, human impacts on ecosystems, conservation, and other factors influencing biological diversity.
A community of discovery
Pursue your research in a doctoral program with the breadth to support questions across the biological sciences. You will join active research communities in areas including ecosystem ecology, infectious disease, physiology, and evolutionary ecology while developing specialized expertise in the area that aligns with your interests.
Your experience can extend beyond your primary research area and beyond the university. Through interdisciplinary collaboration and opportunities to connect with scientists outside academia, you will encounter different approaches to biological research and gain perspectives that broaden your understanding of the field. You will also develop the ability to communicate complex scientific ideas to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, connect your research to broader scientific questions, and contribute confidently to the scientific community.
Turn discovery into impact
A Biology PhD prepares you for research and leadership roles across academia, government, industry, conservation, and other scientific settings. Graduates pursue careers as researchers, professors, government and industry scientists, conservation scientists, ecologists, environmental consultants, and scientific leaders.
Whether you are generating new knowledge, informing policy and practice, teaching future scientists, or leading research initiatives, you will use advanced research, quantitative analysis, and communication skills to contribute to discovery and address complex questions in the biological sciences.
Explore the unknown
Research in the Biology PhD spans questions across the biological sciences, giving you opportunities to investigate living systems at multiple scales. Your work might examine processes within individual organisms, interactions among species, the dynamics of populations and communities, or patterns across entire ecosystems.
Working with faculty mentors, you will connect biological theory with empirical research while developing expertise in the methods and quantitative approaches most relevant to your area of study. You will design and conduct original research, analyze and interpret complex data, and place your findings within broader scientific contexts. Through your dissertation and other research experiences, you willl contribute new knowledge while developing the independence and scientific perspective needed for a career in biological research.
Graduate contact
Questions about the Biology PhD, research opportunities, or finding a faculty mentor? Contact AskBioGrad@nau.edu for guidance and more information about the program.

Admission requirements
Individual program admission requirements over and above admission to NAU are required.
All applicants are expected to make email contact with potential faculty members in the department BEFORE APPLYING. Applicants should only apply if a mentor agrees to support the applicant.
Essay/Letter of Intent/Personal Statement*
One of the following:
An earned thesis-based MS degree in a biological or related science
Demonstrated research ability by being a responsible author on a scientific, peer-reviewed publication (journal article)
Have equivalent credentials to the above, which may include considerable relevant research experience, average GRE scores above the 70th national percentile in Verbal, Quantitative, and Writing Ability, experience presenting scientific papers as an author at regional, national, or international scientific meetings, with reference letters attesting to the student's performance and responsibility for the science reported at such venues.
Knowledge of biology at the baccalaureate level.
